union.summary: Lone-dash relaxation is not scoped to list context, so top-level single-dash setext headings (`Title\n-`) stop rendering as <h2>
union.evidence:
`const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` … `if (pos >= max && !isLoneDash)` unconditionally rejects a one-character `-` underline regardless of `state.blkIndent` / whether we are inside a list item. For input `Title\n-` at top level (blkIndent 0): upstream lheading sets level=2 → `

Title

`; with this rule the underline is skipped, the terminator chain then hits `wrappedList`, whose guard (`silent && parentType==='paragraph' && isEmptyBulletLine`) is satisfied because sCount[1]=0 >= blkIndent=0, so the paragraph terminates and the non-silent `list` rule builds an empty item — output becomes `

Title

`. A single `-` is a valid CommonMark setext H2 underline, and issue #517 is about an *indented, nested* empty bullet, so the relaxation could have been gated on being inside a list item / blkIndent > 0. The added tests only cover `Heading\n---` (multi-dash), and the task doc's own planned 'top-level lone dash' test is absent from preview.test.ts, so the regression is uncovered.

union.summary: `isEmptyBulletLine` accepts `*` and `+`, widening the paragraph-interrupt deviation beyond the documented lone `-`
union.evidence:
`if (marker !== DASH && marker !== 0x2a /* * */ && marker !== 0x2b /* + */) return false;` — the `lheading` relaxation only covers `-`, but the `list` interrupt relaxation covers all three bullet markers. Consequence: `foo *` and `foo +` (and `foo * `) previously stayed inside the paragraph as lazy text (`

foo *

`, since CommonMark forbids an empty bullet from interrupting a paragraph and `hr` needs 3 markers); they now terminate the paragraph and emit `
`. That contradicts docs/design/notes/notes.md, which describes the deviation as scoped to 'a lone single `-` (the empty-bullet shape)'. Nothing in the added tests covers `*`/`+`.

union.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` diverges from upstream lheading's `.trim()` for non-ASCII whitespace
union.evidence: `const content = asciiTrim(state.getLines(...))` with `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g`. markdown-it's `rules_block/lheading` uses `String.prototype.trim()`, which also strips Unicode whitespace (U+00A0 NBSP, U+2028/29, U+FEFF, other Zs). So for `Heading \n===` this copy keeps the trailing NBSP in the heading's inline content where stock markdown-it would drop it — a silent behavioral divergence in a rule that is supposed to be a faithful mirror. The accompanying comment ('ASCII whitespace trimmed by markdown-it's own `asciiTrim`') also appears to describe a helper markdown-it does not have, which is what makes the divergence easy to miss.

union.summary: `getRuleFn` throws from module-initialization scope, so an internals change turns a degraded feature into a hard import failure of the whole preview module
union.evidence: `const rule = ruler.__rules__.find((r) => r.name === name); if (!rule) throw new Error(...)`. `listEmptyBulletPlugin` is invoked by `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` at top level of preview.ts (module side effect, no try/catch), and `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', ...)` likewise throws 'Parser rule not found' if the name is gone. If markdown-it renames/reshapes the private `__rules__` registry (or a plugin removes `list`), importing preview.ts throws and the entire notes preview fails to load rather than just losing the #517 nicety. A defensive fallback (skip the wrapping) would keep the failure local.

union.summary: Hard-coded `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote']` overwrites whatever alt chain `list` actually had at plugin-apply time
union.evidence: `md.block.ruler.at('list', wrappedList, { alt: ['paragraph', 'reference', 'blockquote'] });` restores the alt chain from a literal instead of reading the existing entry's `alt` (which `getRuleFn` is already positioned to return alongside `fn`). `listEmptyBulletPlugin` is applied last in preview.ts, after taskLists, katexPlugin and detailsPlugin; any alt entry one of those (or a future plugin, or a future markdown-it version) added to `list` is silently dropped, and `list` would stop terminating that block type. Reading and reusing the current `alt` array removes the coupling.

union.summary: Silent shortcut returns `true` without replicating the stock list rule's own indent guards, so it can claim a line where no list can actually start
union.evidence: `if (silent && state.parentType === 'paragraph' && isEmptyBulletLine(state, startLine)) return true;` bypasses `originalList` entirely. `isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `sCount[line] >= blkIndent`; the real `list` rule additionally bails on `state.sCount[startLine] - state.blkIndent >= 4` (code block) and on the `state.listIndent >= 0 && sCount - listIndent >= 4 && sCount < blkIndent` lazy-continuation case. Today those combinations are unreachable because every caller of the 'paragraph' terminator chain (`paragraph`, this `lheading` copy, `reference`) `continue`s on `sCount - blkIndent > 3`, but the wrapper is now the contract for any future/plugin caller of that chain: a 4+-space-indented lone bullet would terminate the paragraph while the following non-silent pass refuses to build a list, leaving a stray `-` paragraph or indented code where lazy text was expected. Mirroring the two guards inside `isEmptyBulletLine` would make the shortcut agree with the rule it front-runs.

union.summary: `at('lheading', lheadingRule)` is called without options, which clears that rule's alt chain
union.evidence: `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule);` — the change's own lessons doc notes that `Ruler.at(name, fn, options)` replaces `alt` with `options.alt || []`, and it compensates for `list` but not for `lheading`. In markdown-it 14 `lheading` is registered with no alt list, so this is a no-op there; if the installed version (the docs claim 'markdown-it 14.3.0') registers `lheading` with any alt membership, replacing it here silently removes it and `lheading` stops terminating that block type. Passing the existing `alt` back, as done for `list`, would make this robust rather than version-dependent.

union.summary: `isLoneDash` disables single-dash setext headings everywhere, not just inside list items — `Title\n-` loses its `<h2>` and emits a stray empty bullet
union.evidence:
Line 105: `const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` and line 107 `if (pos >= max && !isLoneDash)`. The guard has no context condition (no check that the dash line is indented deeper than the paragraph, or that `state.parentType`/`state.listIndent` indicates we are inside a list item). Consequence for top-level input `Title\n-`: lheadingRule declines the underline, the terminator loop then calls the wrapped `list` (which returns true for the lone `-`), lheading returns false, `paragraph` consumes `Title` and stops at line 1, and the non-silent `list` rule builds an empty item. Output becomes `

Title

` instead of `

Title

` — the heading is silently downgraded AND the `-` character disappears from the rendered text. Issue #517 only concerns an *indented* empty bullet under a list item; nothing in the fix restricts the deviation to that shape. The tests only cover the multi-dash form (`Heading\n---`), so this regression is untested.

union.summary: Paragraph-interrupt relaxation accepts `*`/`+` and applies to any paragraph, so a literal marker character in body text is silently dropped from the rendered output
union.evidence:
`wrappedList` (lines 182-191) returns `true` for *any* line satisfying `isEmptyBulletLine`, and `isEmptyBulletLine` (line 39) accepts `-`, `*` and `+`, with the only positional constraint being `state.sCount[line] >= state.blkIndent` (line 32). CommonMark/markdown-it deliberately renders `foo\n*` as `

foo\n*

` (an empty bullet may not interrupt a paragraph). With this plugin the paragraph terminates and the non-silent `list` rule builds an empty item, so the output is `

foo

` — the `*` (or `+`, or `-`) glyph the user typed is no longer rendered anywhere. That is user-visible content loss in ordinary prose, well beyond the documented deviation (docs/design/notes/notes.md describes only 'a lone single `-`'), and there is no test for the `*`/`+` or top-level cases.

union.summary: `isEmptyBulletLine` omits the guards the real `list` rule applies, so the silent 'yes' can disagree with what the non-silent `list` rule will do
union.evidence: `isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `state.sCount[line] < state.blkIndent` (line 32). markdown-it's `list` rule additionally rejects `state.sCount[line] - state.blkIndent >= 4` (indented code block) and the `state.listIndent >= 0 && sCount - listIndent >= 4 && sCount < blkIndent` special case. So `wrappedList` can report 'this empty bullet terminates the paragraph' for a line that non-silent `list` will refuse, after which `code`/`paragraph` claims it instead — the paragraph is split for nothing. Today this is masked only because `paragraph`/`lheadingRule` `continue` on lines with `sCount - blkIndent > 3` before consulting terminators (line 86); the invariant is implicit and any future caller (another plugin registering `alt: ['paragraph']`, or a rule that sets `parentType = 'paragraph'`) reaches the unguarded path. Mirroring list's own two guards inside `isEmptyBulletLine` would make silent and non-silent agree by construction.

union.summary: Re-registration hard-codes `list`'s `alt` chain and reads markdown-it's private `__rules__`; both fail silently/at import time if internals or another plugin differ
union.evidence: Line 197-199 calls `md.block.ruler.at('list', wrappedList, { alt: ['paragraph', 'reference', 'blockquote'] })`, restoring a literal copy of upstream's alt list rather than the value actually in effect. Any plugin loaded earlier that added to `list`'s alt chain (or a markdown-it version whose chain differs) has its entry silently dropped, and `list` stops acting as a terminator for that chain — a quiet rendering bug with no error. Compounding it, `getRuleFn` (lines 207-213) reaches into the undocumented `ruler.__rules__` and `throw`s `markdown-it block rule not found` on mismatch; because `preview.ts` calls `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` at module scope, that throw happens at import time and takes down the entire notes preview module rather than degrading. Reading the existing alt chain from `__rules__` (already being accessed) and passing it back would remove the duplication risk.

union.summary: `asciiTrim` is narrower than the `.trim()` upstream `lheading` uses, so setext heading content with non-ASCII whitespace is trimmed differently
union.evidence: Lines 19-23 define `ASCII_TRIM_RE` over `[\x09-\x0d\x20]` and line 134 applies it to `state.getLines(...)`. markdown-it 14's `rules_block/lheading.mjs` uses JS `String.prototype.trim()`, which also strips U+00A0, U+2028/9, U+FEFF etc. A setext heading whose content begins/ends with a NBSP therefore keeps that character here but not upstream. Also, the comment claims this re-creates "markdown-it's own `asciiTrim`"; I could not find such an export in markdown-it's public or common utils, so the stated justification for diverging from `.trim()` looks unverified.

union.summary: Task checklist contradicts the change it ships (all implementation steps left unchecked)
union.evidence: Lines 60-65 list `- [ ] Add packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts`, `- [ ] Wire it into preview.ts`, `- [ ] Unit tests in preview.test.ts`, `- [ ] Note the deviation in docs/design/notes/notes.md` as not done, yet all four are present in this same diff. The stale state makes the doc an unreliable record of what was actually completed.

union.summary: Could not verify that the notes preview is the only renderer of note markdown; if note content is rendered anywhere else, the same text renders differently in the two places
union.evidence: The plugin is installed only on the module-level `md` in `packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts` (diff line adding `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)`), and the design note calls the deviation 'notes-preview-only'. If any other path renders note markdown (export, share/print view, frontend package, server-side render), `- 1\n  -` yields `<h2>` there and a nested empty bullet here — the same document rendering inconsistently, which is a correctness/round-trip hazard rather than a style choice. I could not confirm or refute this because the repository working tree was not available to me.
